study: Meng, Wang, Yang & Zhang, Education Competition and Fertility Intention: Evidence from China's Private Tutoring Ban
setting: China, nationwide; 2021 'Double Reduction' private tutoring ban
policy_or_shock: The 2021 ban on for-profit academic tutoring. Policy INTENSITY = per-capita number of tutoring institutions in 2016, five years pre-policy, from administrative firm registrations
design: (a) survey experiment eliciting fertility intentions under with/without-policy scenarios, within-subject with individual FE plus a between-subject arm; (b) city-level DID on ACTUAL birth rates, 2016-19 avg and 2020 (Census) vs 2023 (319 cities) and 2024 (204 cities), city and year FE, controls for lagged GDP pc, housing price, per-student public education expenditure, COVID cases; SEs clustered by city
return_separated: YES — a tutoring ban does not change the RETURN to human capital; it changes the investment required to hold a given rank. The paper's own decomposition separates perceived competition from monetary and time cost, and its footnote defines perceived competition as how hard it is for one's child to maintain academic ranking, which determines elite high-school and university admission. That is the reference standard, not the return.
own_income_held: YES — individual FE in the within-subject design; city FE and lagged GDP pc in the DID
outcome: expected total fertility (stated); city-level birth rate per 1,000 (realized)
effect: Ban raises expected total fertility by 7-8%, larger where policy intensity is higher. DID on actual birth rates: cities with higher policy intensity had significantly greater increases relative to average-intensity cities. Channel decomposition: PRIMARY driver is perceived reduction in educational competition (45% of parents expected others to cut tutoring), then parental health / parent-child relationship (>0.5 SD), then time (-0.69 h/day, -18.1%) and money (-275 RMB/month, -34.5%).
sign_vs_c2f: SUPPORTS — the mechanism operates and the competition channel dominates the pure cost channel
routing: C.2.f's own. The cost sub-channel (money and time) is C.2.b's estimand and is reported separately by the authors, so the two are separable here rather than jointly claimed.

study: Zhou, Shao & Zhang, The impact of China's 'Double Reduction' policy on the fertility and education investment behaviour of Chinese households
setting: China; CFPS 2018 micro-data for the empirical section, national calibration for the model
policy_or_shock: Same 2021 'Double Reduction' policy — but SIMULATED, not evaluated
design: TWO PARTS. (III) IV estimate on CFPS 2018, adults 18-50 with children in compulsory education, n=3,481; OLS/2SLS, Poisson/IV-Poisson, Probit/IV-Probit. Instruments = average shadow-education expenditure of students one year older and one year younger in the same county (peer-effect IV). (IV-VI) a calibrated heterogeneous-agent model with endogenous fertility and private education investment, incorporating the separate urban/rural high-school entrance exam admission mechanism, solved with a new DeepHAM+DIRECT algorithm; the policy effect is a SIMULATION.
return_separated: NO — the empirical IV does not separate the return from the reference standard. The MODEL is explicitly positional (rank-based zhongkao admission), but the model is not an estimate.
own_income_held: UNCLEAR — income is a control in the IV specification, but the instrument is county-level peer expenditure, which is plausibly correlated with county income
outcome: ideal number of children; second-child intention (binary)
effect: Empirical: shadow-education expenditure per child has a statistically significant NEGATIVE effect on parents' fertility intentions across OLS, 2SLS, Poisson, IV-Poisson, Probit and IV-Probit. Simulated: regulating shadow education 'can boost fertility and reduce parents' burdens, with efficacy escalating proportionally to regulatory stringency'.
sign_vs_c2f: SUPPORTS on the empirical arm; the policy result is model-generated and carries no identification
routing: SPLIT. The Double Reduction result is a calibrated simulation and must NOT be pooled with C2F0428's estimate of the same policy. The empirical arm is an expenditure exposure instrumented by county peer expenditure -- and the exclusion restriction is doing heavy work, because county-level peer spending IS the reference standard this chapter says is the mechanism, so it plausibly affects intentions directly. Flag for risk of bias.
